bundle.author: swain
bundle.title: Pull base images from ECR Public with a login
bundle.body:
Docker builds keep failing with 429 Too Many Requests because base images are pulled anonymously from Docker Hub, which limits pulls per IP, and GitHub runners share IPs. Pulling anonymously from ECR Public instead was tried and also 429'd (#2194), for the same reason.

Logged-in ECR Public pulls are limited per AWS account rather than per IP, so this moves every FROM line, and the buildx builder image, to public.ecr.aws/docker/library and logs in to ECR Public before each image build. Local builds are unaffected: one developer pulling anonymously stays well under the limit, so nobody has to log in to build an image on their laptop.

Main builds already hold the deploy role, which can log in. gp-ai's PR build holds no AWS credentials on purpose (#2146), so it assumes github-actions-ecr-public-login, a role that can mint an ECR Public login token and nothing else.

Depends on thegoodparty/ops#291, which creates that role. Until it is merged and deployed, the gp-ai image build on this PR fails at the assume-role step. Merge this only after #291 is applied.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes CI authentication and every service image base layer; misconfigured IAM or registry paths would break all Docker builds until fixed, but runtime app logic is unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Stops CI Docker builds from hitting anonymous registry rate limits (429)** by sourcing all `FROM` base images and the Buildx BuildKit driver from **ECR Public** (`public.ecr.aws/docker/library/...`) instead of Docker Hub, and logging into ECR Public before every image build.
> 
> Workflow updates add **`Login to Amazon ECR Public`** (`registry-type: public`) in `gp-ai.yml`, `gp-api.yml`, and `release.yml`, and point Buildx at `public.ecr.aws/vend/moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1`. **gp-ai PR builds** now assume a dedicated IAM role (`github-actions-ecr-public-login`) so they can authenticate for public pulls without the deploy role or ECR push access; main/push paths still use the existing deploy role for private ECR.
> 
> Dockerfiles for **gp-api**, **election-api**, and all **gp-ai** services switch their Node/Python base images to the ECR Public library mirrors. **`docs/deployment.md`** documents the pattern and credential split.
> 
> **Dependency:** gp-ai PR image builds need the ops role from `thegoodparty/ops#291` deployed before this merges.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit cdd3c4b92a0935d483401c143d3b8632add8c663. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

--- a/.github/workflows/gp-ai.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/gp-ai.yml
@@ -28,7 +28,7 @@ env:
   AWS_REGION: us-west-2

   # Static, so the image tag does not depend on the ECR login step. That is
-  # what lets a pull request build without AWS credentials at all.
+  # what lets a pull request build without the deploy role.
   ECR_REGISTRY: 333022194791.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
   SUBTREE: packages/gp-ai
 
@@ -279,17 +279,19 @@ jobs:
             echo "build-args=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           fi
 
-      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
-        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
+      # Base images and the buildkit image come from ECR Public. Anonymous
+      # pulls there are limited per IP and shared runners hit 429s; logged in,
+      # the limit is per account. So every build logs in to ECR Public. A pull
+      # request builds to validate the Dockerfile and throws the image away, so
+      # it gets a role that can only log in to ECR Public, never the deploy
+      # role and its ECR push.
+      - name: Configure AWS Credentials (ECR Public login)
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
         with:
-          driver-opts: |
-            image=moby/buildkit:latest
-            network=host
+          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::333022194791:role/github-actions-ecr-public-login
+          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
 
-      # Only where something is actually pushed. A pull request builds to
-      # validate the Dockerfile and throws the image away, and every base
-      # image here is public, so a PR run needs no AWS access. It used to take
-      # credentials unconditionally and hold ECR push it never exercised.
       - name: Configure AWS Credentials
         if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref_name == 'main'
         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
@@ -297,10 +299,22 @@ jobs:
           role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_ROLE_ARN }}
           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
 
+      - name: Login to Amazon ECR Public
+        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2
+        with:
+          registry-type: public
+
       - name: Login to Amazon ECR
         if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref_name == 'main'
         uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2
 
+      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
+        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
+        with:
+          driver-opts: |
+            image=public.ecr.aws/vend/moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1
+            network=host
+
       # Build on PRs too (catches a broken Dockerfile before merge) but only
       # push from main — a PR pushing SHA tags would litter ECR with images for
       # commits that never land.

+          registry-type: public

+### Base images
+
+Every Dockerfile `FROM`, and the buildx builder image, pulls from ECR Public
+(`public.ecr.aws/docker/library/<image>:<tag>`), never Docker Hub. Anonymous
+pulls from either are limited per IP, and shared GitHub runners kept failing
+with `429 Too Many Requests`. Logged-in ECR Public pulls are limited per AWS
+account, so every job that builds an image logs in to ECR Public first
+(`aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login` with `registry-type: public`). Main runs log
+in with `vars.AWS_ROLE_ARN`. gp-ai's pull request build, which otherwise holds
+no AWS credentials, assumes `github-actions-ecr-public-login`, which can only
+mint that login token (defined in `thegoodparty/ops`). Local builds need no
+login.

output.summary: This PR switches every Dockerfile `FROM` line and the Buildx builder image from Docker Hub to ECR Public (`public.ecr.aws/docker/library/…`), and adds authenticated ECR Public login steps to the gp-ai, gp-api, and release workflows to avoid the per-IP anonymous pull rate limits (429s) that shared GitHub runners were hitting. For gp-ai PR builds, a dedicated minimal IAM role (`github-actions-ecr-public-login`) is assumed instead of the deploy role, matching the PR description. The scout flagged four areas: (1) `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest` lines remaining in Python Dockerfiles — verified as non-blocking because GHCR public image limits are much more generous and these pulls predate the PR; (2) the unconditional ECR Public login step in gp-ai.yml — verified safe because the workflow's only two triggers (`pull_request` and `push` to `main`) are exhaustively covered by the two conditional credential steps; (3) election-api using plain `docker build` instead of buildx — verified fine because `amazon-ecr-login` writes to `~/.docker/config.json`, which plain `docker build` reads; (4) the hardcoded IAM role ARN — verified as intentional since it is a separate, minimal-permission role and the ARN is not a secret. No blocker-grade issues were found.
